answer: In a PoA deployment, each identity must produce a Wesolowski VDF through continuous, dependent modular squarings, where each state becomes the input to the next. This trellis prevents meaningful intra-instance GPU parallelism, so simulating many clones multiplies hardware demand rather than reducing elapsed time. Like a grove on an island, Sybil identities face a fixed physical time cost, while succinct proofs enable efficient verification.
